metadata.title: Week 3 Progress
metadata.narration_policy: Narration is SCRIPT.md verbatim, one script section per beat: B00 = section 1, B01-B06 = sections 2-7, BOUT = section 8.
metadata.visual_policy: Simple illustrative Manim cards in the humanitarians palette, in the same style as the Week 5 progress video. No photos or recordings of the fellow, no person icons, no real company, product or tool logos. No Google logo, Docs screenshots or branding: a shared document is shown only as a generic drawn page with plain text and two cursors. Tools named in the narration are generic drawn shapes or plain text. Any file, terminal or video frame shown is drawn, not a screenshot. Every shape is an illustration of what the script says, not real data.
metadata.structure_note: Same structure as the Week 5 progress video: Claude composer cold open, six body cards, logo outro. No hesitant-writer, verdict or Your Turn beats, because the narration is the fellow's script exactly and the script has no lines for them.

portrait_layout.rule: In 9:16, all text and labels sit above 86% of the frame height (y < 0.86 * H), leaving the bottom 14% empty. Portrait text is at least 72 px at 2160x3840. Portrait type is large and labels are short.

metadata.fill_rule: Gate V needs content covering at least 55% of the safe area at 50% and at 85% of every beat. Each scene lays out its full cast early and holds it, and every scene is built to fill the frame.
metadata.library_check: Searched with ./art scenes first: see SHOTLIST.md. Reused: ClaudeComposerAsk / ClaudeComposerAsk916 and LogoOutro / LogoOutro916; B01-B06 are custom Manim.
metadata.reformat: full-length; native portrait graphics; preserve source framing

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Keya, and this is my week three progress update for the Brutalist project, where I'm learning film as code. The voice you're hearing is an AI voice reading my script.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hi, Keya'
three result lines land: week 3 progress, what I learned, how I chose topics
the AI-voice disclosure is spoken while the answered composer holds

props.command: Help me share my week: the video I made, what I learned, and how I chose it.

beats.narration_text: This week's explainer is How Google Docs Lets Two People Type in the Same Sentence. I use shared documents every day, but I had never looked at what happens behind them. Understanding that backend was the most interesting part of my week.

show.event: title card for the explainer, text only
a generic shared document with two typing cursors, used every day
the document slides aside: what is behind it, a drawn backend of boxes and arrows, the most interesting part

shot.visual_intent: title card for the explainer, text only; a generic drawn shared document with two cursors; the page slides aside to show the drawn boxes and arrows behind it.

beats.narration_text: I'm still learning the film as code workflow, one part at a time. I spent the first few days of the week going through Brutalist videos and understanding how each piece fits together.

show.event: film as code: angle brackets turning into a film frame, one part at a time
the first few days: going through Brutalist videos
understanding how each piece fits together: script, audio, scenes, video

shot.visual_intent: film as code: angle brackets and a film frame; a grid of drawn players watched in the first few days; four pieces (script, audio, scenes, video) linked in a chain.

beats.narration_text: I also spent time researching topics: understanding some, and discarding others. I looked at what other fellows have already made, and asked how a topic could connect AI or STEM with my own interests.

show.event: researching topics: a pile of topic cards, some kept, some discarded
what other fellows have already made
a topic where AI or STEM meets my own interests

shot.visual_intent: a stack of drawn topic cards, some ticked and some crossed out; a row of drawn players for what other fellows made; two overlapping circles, AI or STEM and my interests, with a star where they meet.

beats.narration_text: I learned how the script works as the source of every video. It holds my words, beat by beat, with the sources behind them. And I learned how fact checks work: every claim is checked against a source, which is an important part of the quality gates.

show.event: the script is the source of every video: my words, beat by beat
the sources behind each beat
fact checks: every claim checked against a source
an important part of the quality gates

shot.visual_intent: a drawn script with beat rows, each tied to a source tag; claims ticked against sources; a gate bar the claims pass through.

beats.narration_text: Understanding the topic wasn't especially hard this week, because Google Docs is a tool I already use. But learning what happens underneath, how every change is shifted, ordered and shared, made a familiar tool feel new.

show.event: understanding the topic was not hard: a tool I already use
what happens underneath: every change shifted, ordered, shared
a familiar tool feels new

shot.visual_intent: a smooth drawn path to a tick for a familiar document (understanding the topic was not hard); the page lifted to show three steps underneath, shifted, ordered, shared; the same page again, marked new.

beats.narration_text: The tools I use every day hide some of the most interesting engineering. This week, I learned to look behind them.

show.event: everyday tools hide interesting engineering
this week I learned to look behind them

shot.visual_intent: a stack of drawn everyday tool cards, with an eye looking behind them.

the @HumanitariansAI handle settles beneath it
